name: Quiet Meadow
pitch: The child spends a soft, slow day in Hazelbrook Meadow with three woodland friends, wondering about one small, big question together until the answer turns up in a quiet, unexpected way.
setting: Hazelbrook Meadow, a gentle valley of tall whispering grass, an old oak with a little round door between its roots, a slow stream with flat stepping stones, a hill where the wind is always kind, and a bench made from a fallen log

supportingCast.name: Bramble
supportingCast.role: small, shy friend who worries about things
supportingCast.look: a little round hedgehog with soft brown spines, a pale face, tiny paws, and a too-long knitted scarf the color of moss

supportingCast.name: Old Willa
supportingCast.role: wise, unhurried friend who thinks before she speaks
supportingCast.look: a tall grey goose with a gentle face, half-moon spectacles on a ribbon, and a small cloth bag over one wing

supportingCast.name: Puddle
supportingCast.role: cheerful, curious friend full of questions
supportingCast.look: a young otter with sleek honey-brown fur, round ears, bright eyes, and a sprig of clover tucked behind one ear

storyBeats: a friend helps in a small way
powerIdeas: The child's kindness, patience or way of noticing small things is what helps; one favorite thing can appear as a gentle, meaningful detail.

artDirection.mood: quiet, tender, warm and unhurried, with soft light and plenty of white space

contentRules: gentle and calm throughout; no villains, chases or peril
feelings (sad, worried, cross, shy) are welcome and treated kindly
friends help in small, practical ways

starters.title: Where the Stream Goes
starters.idea: Puddle wonders where the slow stream goes, but tall reeds block the view. Following the bank ends at a wall of reeds, and Bramble worries it goes somewhere scary. Old Willa's leaf boats float ahead, the friends climb the gentle hill, and from the top they see the stream ends in a round, quiet pond that holds the sky.

starters.title: The First Frost
starters.idea: Bramble is worried about the first cold night. A pile of leaves blows away and the old oak's door won't shut. The child notices how close everyone sits on the log bench, they share Bramble's long scarf and a warm cup, and the frost turns the meadow sparkly instead of scary.
